THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ORDERS THIS DAY,
B.M.SHYAM PRASAD J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
JUDGMENT
This appeal is by the claimant in MVC No.905/2015 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal No-XIII, Vijayapura (for short, 'the Tribunal').

sentences.text: The appellant has suffered amputation of a toe in the lower limb in the road traffic accident on 09.04.2015, and the Tribunal has awarded a total sum of Rs.2,09,339/- as compensation along with interest at the rate of 9% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

However, there are obvious errors in the Tribunal's computation,

Sri Koujalagi Chandrakant Laxman, the learned counsel for the appellant, and Sri Mohd. Abdul Quayum, the learned standing counsel for the Insurer, are heard in the light of the submissions that the accident and the Insurer's liability are not disputed, and the nature of the injuries suffered by the appellant is also not disputed.
The total sum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is Rs.2,09,339/, but the actual total compensation on calculation of amounts under different heads comes to Rs.2,27,339/-.
They submit that the only question for consideration is whether there must be enhancement in the compensation awarded as a consequence of reassessment of the disability.
3. The Tribunal, in consideration of the doctor's evidence [but who has not treated the appellant],
has assessed the appellant's disability at 6.66%.
The doctor's evidence is that the disability is between 20% to 25%.
There is nothing on record to indicate that the appellant, as a consequence of amputation of a toe, has suffered any functional disability.

In fact, if the case of the appellant is that he is engaged in a business, and there is nothing to indicate functional disability because of the amputation, the compensation awarded under such head is reasonable and requires no enhancement.

4. At this stage, Sri Koujalagi Chandrakant Laxman submits that the evidence is that the appellant has taken treatment over a period of time in two different hospitals with a further follow up treatment.
But the NC: 2023:KHC-K:5445-DB Tribunal has granted only a sum of Rs.5,000/- under hospitalization expenses observing that this would indicate compensation towards transportation and nourishment.

It is seen that a sum of Rs.28,639/- is awarded towards medical expenses based on the medical bills produced but then, Rs.5,000/- would be very conservative if the appellant has undergone hospitalization in two different institutions especially when there is no award towards loss of amenities.
5.

On a holistic consideration of the above circumstances, this Court is of the considered view that there can only be a global sum as additional compensation, and this Court is of the further view that a sum of Rs.50,000/- could be just and proper.

Hence, the appeal is allowed modifying the Tribunal's impugned judgment and award dated 25.06.2019 granting a global sum of Rs.50,000/-
as additional compensation.
